The day's crypto news is a mixture of market positioning, fund flows, policy updates, and company decisions. The headlines below are worth reading for the detail behind them, not just the reaction on a price chart.

What is moving the conversation

Bitcoin tops $65,000 with US inflation data due this week. Every major except XRP is green on the week, with BTC, ether and BNB each up nearly 3% as global stocks trade near a record. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

XRP is getting left behind in the crypto bounce even as ETFs keep attracting investor money. The token fell 5% last week while BTC, ETH and SOL climbed. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Is Clarity's delay a blessing in disguise?: State of Crypto. The crypto industry is angry and disappointed that the Senate is not holding a procedural vote on the Clarity Act this month, but that isn't the worst possible outcome. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Hyperliquid’s RWA perps boom is eating into the revenue that backs HYPE. Revenue has fallen four quarters running while open interest hit a record high. The gap is a fee-sharing program that hands half the platform's volume to outside builders. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Bitcoin investors pour $853 million into spot ETFs. BlackRock’s IBIT claims the bulk. Bitcoin ETFs recorded $853.54 million in net inflows last week, the strongest since mid-April, with BlackRock’s IBIT taking the bulk. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Crypto is going through a massive dot-com style shakeout as over 100 projects fold in 2026. An industry-wide reckoning is weeding out unsustainable startups, leaving behind only the protocols with real cash flow and actual users. Readers should check the original report before treating the headline as a confirmed change in the market.

Market context

Bitcoin is around $64,963 with a +0.34% 24-hour move, while Ether is around $1,915.29 with a +0.16% move. Those figures are a snapshot, not a forecast. The useful question is whether the move is supported by spot demand, volume, and a clear change in the news.

When the market is quiet, leverage and liquidity can matter as much as direction. A small headline can move price quickly when traders are positioned too closely on one side.

What to watch next

  • New ETF creations and redemptions.
  • Futures open interest and funding rates.
  • Fresh regulatory text or official statements.
  • Security warnings, outages, or custody changes.
  • Whether the reported developments become live products rather than announcements.

The fairest reading today is cautious attention. There are real developments in the industry, but none should be stretched into a guaranteed market direction.
